description: Learn best practices for structuring your API, handling versioning, and deploying to production.

slides.title: API Structuring
slides.content:
# APIRouter 🗺️

If you put 100 endpoints in `main.py`, your file will be 3000 lines long and impossible to read.
FastAPI provides `APIRouter` to split your API across multiple files.

```python_not
# routers/users.py
from fastapi import APIRouter

# Create a router specifically for users
router = APIRouter(prefix="/users", tags=["users"])

@router.get("/")  # This actually maps to /users/
def get_users(): pass
```

slides.title: Including Routers
slides.content:
# Connecting Routers to Main 🧩

Once you have multiple router files, you simply "include" them in your main `app` instance.

```python_not
# main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from routers import users, products

app = FastAPI()

# Mount the routers onto the main app
app.include_router(users.router)
app.include_router(products.router)
```
This keeps your codebase clean, modular, and easy to maintain!

slides.title: API Versioning
slides.content:
# Versioning your API 🏷️

Once people are using your API, you cannot make breaking changes (like changing a field name from `firstName` to `first_name`), or you will crash their apps!

To fix this, you use **Versioning**.
The easiest way in FastAPI is to use the `prefix` in `APIRouter`.

```python_not
# Mount v1 routers
app.include_router(users_v1.router, prefix="/api/v1")

# Mount v2 routers (with breaking changes)
app.include_router(users_v2.router, prefix="/api/v2")
```
Now `/api/v1/users` and `/api/v2/users` can exist simultaneously!

slides.title: Uvicorn and Gunicorn
slides.content:
# The ASGI Servers 🦄

FastAPI is an **ASGI** framework (Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface). It requires an ASGI server to run.

**Uvicorn** is the incredibly fast ASGI server you use for local development: 
`uvicorn main:app --reload`

However, Uvicorn only runs on a single CPU core. If your server has 8 cores, you are wasting 7 of them!

In production, you use **Gunicorn** as a process manager to run *multiple* Uvicorn workers.

slides.title: Running in Production
slides.content:
# The Gunicorn Command 🏭

To run FastAPI in production across multiple CPU cores, use this command:

```bash
gunicorn main:app -w 4 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker
```

- `-w 4`: Start 4 worker processes.
- `-k uvicorn...`: Tell Gunicorn to use Uvicorn classes to handle the async ASGI code.

If one worker crashes, Gunicorn automatically restarts it. Your API stays online!

slides.title: Dockerizing FastAPI
slides.content:
# Deploying with Docker 🐳

The standard way to deploy FastAPI to AWS, Google Cloud, or DigitalOcean is to package it into a Docker container.

Create a `Dockerfile` in your project root:

```dockerfile
# Use the official Python base image
FROM python:3.10-slim

# Set the working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy requirements and install them
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Copy the rest of the code
COPY . .

# Expose port 80
EXPOSE 80

# Command to run the application using Uvicorn directly
# (Or use Gunicorn if running bare-metal without a container orchestrator)
CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "80"]
```

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Summary 🎉

You've completed the FastAPI course!

## Key Takeaways
- ✅ **APIRouter:** Use routers to modularize your code into separate files (`app.include_router`).
- ✅ **Versioning:** Use the `prefix` argument in routers to create `/v1/` and `/v2/` APIs to avoid breaking existing clients.
- ✅ **Uvicorn:** The ultra-fast ASGI server used to run FastAPI.
- ✅ **Gunicorn:** The WSGI server used as a process manager in production to run multiple Uvicorn workers across all CPU cores.
- ✅ **Docker:** Containerize your FastAPI application to make deploying it to the cloud seamless and reliable.
